newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska governor includes tax cut in budget.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska governor includes tax cut in budget.

text.p: Nebraska Gov. Ben Nelson proposed a $4 billion fiscal 1998-99 general fund biennial budget Wednesday that includes cuts in income and property taxes.

In a speech to the legislature, Nelson said the state's projected surplus should be tapped for tax cuts. He proposed a 5.5 percent across-the-board income tax cut, as well as a $160 annual property tax credit for homeowners.
The cuts are estimated to cost $122 million in fiscal 1998 and $111 million in fiscal 1999, according to the state's budget office.

The tax relief package would be funded through projected beginning balances of $206 million in fiscal 1998 and $159 million in fiscal 1999, while maintaining a cash reserve fund balance of nearly $41 million in each of the fiscal years.
Nelson also said he would support a one-year study of a local option property tax relief measure. The measure would allow voters to approve a local income tax to fund property tax relief.

The governor pointed out that last year the legislature took steps to reduce property taxes. Those included a two percent cap on local government budget increases in fiscal 1997 and a limit on their proerty tax levies starting in 1999.
Nelson said his budget would increase state aid to schools by $47.3 million over the bienium.
